question: Can networks with identical input-output behavior have radically different internal organization, with fixed-objective gradient training tending toward fractured, redundant, entangled circuits while open-ended human-guided evolution yields unified, factored, and adaptable representations?

key_findings.claim: The paper introduces fractured entangled representation as a hypothesis and unified factored representation as an aspirational ideal, not as formally defined or validated quantities.
key_findings.evidence: FER is described as one concept being split into disconnected context-specific mechanisms whose functions are also inappropriately coupled; UFR is one reusable mechanism per unitary concept with independent capabilities factored into modules. The authors explicitly label the article a position paper, state that perfect UFR may be unattainable, and do not propose a singular algorithm, theorem, or numerical FER score.

key_findings.claim: For three selected Picbreeder images, an evolved CPPN and a gradient-trained replica can render nearly identical 256-by-256 outputs while presenting visibly different neuron activation maps.
key_findings.evidence: The skull, butterfly, and apple evolved networks are layerized into dense sequential architectures without changing their computations. Newly initialized networks with the same layer shapes and activation assignments are trained on all pixel-coordinate/color pairs for 100,000 full-batch iterations. The replicas visually match their targets, whereas rendered hidden maps in the evolved networks show early symmetry or object-part separation and the trained networks show many irregular high-frequency maps.

key_findings.claim: The comparison does not isolate open-ended search from human semantic selection, topology growth, heterogeneous activation functions, sparsity, curriculum, or the objective itself.
key_findings.evidence: Picbreeder users repeatedly choose visually interesting parents, can change goals, and favor symmetry and other human-salient regularities while NEAT grows topology and selects identity, sine, cosine, tanh, sigmoid, or Gaussian activations. The comparator freezes the final layerized architecture, randomizes weights, makes all layer-to-layer connections trainable, and optimizes one pixel MSE target directly. These conditions differ along every factor proposed to cause UFR, so the experiment is an existence contrast rather than a causal attribution to open-endedness or SGD.

key_findings.claim: Weight sweeps make the evolved parameterizations look more semantically editable, but the paper does not quantify typicality, disentanglement, or functional adaptation.
key_findings.evidence: Selected individual weights in evolved skull, butterfly, and apple networks control mouth opening, eye width, wing area, color, apple size, or stem angle, while selected replica weights cause coupled distortions. The authors say displays were chosen to put both methods in their best light and be broadly representative and provide all sweeps externally, but report no distribution over all weights, annotator agreement, semantic-change score, symmetry statistic, OOD task, learning speed, or continual-learning result.

key_findings.claim: PCA and random parameter-direction sweeps address only a small part of the representation-basis ambiguity and do not make FER or UFR identifiable from the represented function.
key_findings.evidence: PCA of one skull replica remains visually disorganized, and four random column-direction sweeps for each network preserve the qualitative contrast. However, PCA is one linear basis; arbitrary function-preserving permutations, positive rescalings, neuron duplication, compensating transformations across adjacent layers, nonlinear coordinate changes, and alternative semantic factorizations remain. Sweeping one matrix column under a random direction is not the same as jointly reparameterizing adjacent layers while preserving the network function.

key_findings.claim: The reported comparator is full-batch gradient descent on every pixel rather than stochastic minibatch training, and it omits simple regularized or symmetry-aware baselines that could directly test the proposed pathology.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C uses all 65,536 pixels in every step, MSE, LeCun initialization, one learning rate, and 100,000 iterations; the apple changes only the learning rate. No weight decay, L1 or group sparsity, pruning and retraining, low-rank constraint, symmetry augmentation, equivariant architecture, curriculum, modular regularizer, architecture search, Adam, or SGD noise ablation is reported. The raw sparse Picbreeder topology fails for three randomized seeds, showing optimization difficulty but not whether conventional objectives necessarily produce FER.

key_findings.claim: The ReLU appendix shows that visually irregular hidden maps are not solely caused by mixed CPPN activations, but it lacks a matched evolved ReLU reference and quantitative analysis.
key_findings.evidence: Separate all-ReLU MLPs trained on the skull, butterfly, and apple display many asymmetric or high-frequency activations. Because Picbreeder's UFR examples depend on the heterogeneous activation family and evolved topology, the appendix compares ReLU replicas only to non-ReLU evolved networks and reports neither semantic sweeps nor controlled accuracy, width, seed, or sparsity comparisons.

key_findings.claim: The GPT and image-generation examples are behavioral anecdotes consistent with context sensitivity, but they cannot establish fractured internal circuits.
key_findings.evidence: The paper contrasts three GPT-3 counting trials across object categories, three GPT-4o sequence-editing trials across numbers and words, and three March-2025 GPT-4o images each for ape versus human extra-thumb prompts. Output asymmetry is also compatible with data frequency, tokenization, instruction ambiguity, sampling, safety or product pipelines, and ordinary capability limitations. The paper performs no model-internal tracing, causal intervention, matched decoding control, replication across current models, or statistical test for these examples.

anchors.section: Shortcut, Othello, arithmetic, and sequence examples
GPT-4o word sequence and extra-thumb discussion

key_findings.claim: The proposed consequences for generalization, creativity, learning, and scaling are motivating conjectures rather than evaluated outcomes.
key_findings.evidence: No CPPN input region is held out, no new image task is learned after the target, no compositional generalization metric is measured, and no continual-learning or creativity protocol is run. Smooth weight perturbations show local parameter editability, which may be useful, but do not demonstrate improved adaptation by an optimizer or transfer to large models. The authors appropriately frame causal mechanisms, mitigation, scale dependence, grokking, curricula, and open-ended LLM training as open questions.

method.core_idea: Use tiny coordinate-to-color image networks whose complete sampled input-output behavior and every hidden unit can be visualized, then contrast an historically evolved Picbreeder parameterization with a directly optimized function-matching replica to motivate a holistic representation-quality hypothesis beyond benchmark loss.
method.mechanism: Picbreeder CPPNs take x, y, radius, and bias inputs and emit HSV color through graph-structured networks evolved by human-guided NEAT with heterogeneous activation functions. Each evolved graph is exactly ported into a layered MLP using identity transport units. A fresh dense network with the same layer dimensions and activations is initialized and optimized for 100,000 full-batch MSE steps on the entire 256-by-256 pixel grid. Hidden activations are rendered as images; selected individual-weight sweeps, PCA features, and random column-direction sweeps are visually compared. The paper then connects those observations to published mechanistic-interpretability findings and a few prompted frontier-model failures.
assumptions: Human-recognizable symmetry and object parts are the relevant ground-truth factors for judging these CPPN representations.
A unitary concept should ideally correspond to one reusable circuit rather than multiple context-specific implementations.
Independent semantic factors should be locally and independently controllable in parameter space.
Visual similarity of hidden activation maps faithfully reflects organization, redundancy, and entanglement.
The evolved Picbreeder solution is close to UFR rather than merely one human-preferred sparse parameterization.
Layerization preserves not just the function but all representation properties relevant to the comparison.
Training on a dense 256-by-256 grid adequately captures the continuous coordinate-to-color function.
A fixed final architecture with direct target MSE is a meaningful stand-in for conventional large-model pretraining.
Full-batch direct optimization is representative of stochastic minibatch SGD despite removing gradient noise.
Semantic editability under single-weight or random-direction sweeps predicts future learning, generalization, and creativity.
PCA and random orthonormal parameter directions sufficiently address the possibility of a hidden alternative feature basis.
Three human-selected Picbreeder artifacts and one displayed trained replica per artifact characterize a systematic optimization tendency.
Behavioral context failures in closed frontier models imply duplicated or entangled internal algorithms rather than other pipeline or data causes.
Open-ended selection, rather than human supervision, activation choice, growing topology, sparsity, or curriculum, is the main source of UFR.
Representations that are more factorized in human semantic coordinates are preferable even if maximum compression or another factorization would support the task equally well.

techniques.role: Makes the sampled behavior of every hidden neuron visible as a two-dimensional activation image.
Uses human-guided topology and activation evolution as the source of open-ended reference solutions.
Ports irregular NEAT graphs into functionally identical sequential MLPs with identity transport neurons.
Trains a fresh dense parameterization to reproduce every sampled pixel of an evolved target.
Displays all per-neuron activation maps layer by layer and marks maps judged novel.
Perturbs one connection to qualitatively inspect whether output variation is semantic and factor-specific.
Projects each layer's activation data onto principal components as one alternative representation basis.
Perturbs a matrix column along random directions to reduce dependence on original single-weight coordinates.
Changes one context in an LLM or image-generation prompt and interprets asymmetric success as possible FER.

evaluations.setting: Picbreeder skull and a dense layerized-architecture replica trained on all 256-by-256 coordinate/color pairs
evaluations.metric: Pixel MSE and qualitative hidden-map organization
evaluations.result: The replica visually matches the skull while evolved activations show early bilateral structure and about 24 maps marked novel; the replica uses many irregular maps across 12 layers.
evaluations.baseline: One historically evolved human-selected Picbreeder CPPN

evaluations.setting: Single-weight perturbations of skull, butterfly, and apple networks
evaluations.metric: Qualitative semantic control and preservation of symmetry or object identity
evaluations.result: Selected evolved weights control mouth, eye, wing, color, body, background, or stem factors; selected replica weights usually alter several factors or introduce distortions.
evaluations.baseline: Directly optimized replica with the same layerized dimensions and activation assignments

evaluations.metric: Output reconstruction plus visual neuron-map and weight-sweep comparison
evaluations.result: The butterfly replica appears to build left and right wings separately and the apple replica entangles body, stem, background, and color; evolved references look sparse and modular.

evaluations.setting: Randomly initialized original sparse skull topology
evaluations.metric: Training loss and final image over 100,000 iterations
evaluations.result: All three seeds remain in visibly poor local optima, motivating the dense layerization used in the main comparison.

evaluations.setting: All-ReLU MLP replicas for skull, butterfly, and apple
evaluations.result: All three still display asymmetric or high-frequency patterns interpreted as FER.
evaluations.baseline: No matched ReLU evolved or explicitly modular reference

evaluations.setting: PCA of the skull replica's layer activations
evaluations.metric: Qualitative visual organization of principal-component maps
evaluations.result: PCA looks somewhat less fractured than raw neuron coordinates but remains less human-organized than the evolved reference.
evaluations.baseline: Raw feature basis and evolved feature maps

evaluations.setting: Four displayed random column-direction sweeps per skull network
evaluations.result: Evolved directions tend to preserve skull-like structure while replica directions cause irregular distortions.
evaluations.baseline: Evolved versus directly optimized parameterization; no aggregate distribution

evaluations.setting: Prompt contrasts on GPT-3 and March-2025 GPT-4o products
evaluations.result: GPT-3 counts office supplies but not animals; GPT-4o edits number positions but not analogous word positions and draws an extra thumb for human but not ape hands.
evaluations.baseline: Near-identical prompt with one semantic context changed

limitations: Author-stated: this is a position paper that proposes neither a singular solution nor a new training algorithm.
Author-stated: the work does not claim Picbreeder is superior to conventional training, and FER may arise under evolutionary or second-order optimization too.
Author-stated: perfect UFR may be unattainable and the role of NEAT versus open-ended human selection is not understood.
Author-stated: more data, grokking, architecture, regularization, curricula, or modified SGD may reduce FER; the experiments do not settle those possibilities.
Reviewer-identified: FER, fracture, redundancy, entanglement, unification, and factorization have no operational definitions, basis-invariant metric, threshold, or falsification criterion.
Reviewer-identified: semantic UFR labels come from author inspection of activation images and selected sweeps without ground-truth factor annotations or blinded human ratings.
Reviewer-identified: three retrospectively selected Picbreeder successes cannot estimate prevalence across the archive, target complexity, user histories, or random search runs.
Reviewer-identified: one displayed directly trained solution per artifact cannot establish a tendency across initializations; training curves do not report representation variation across seeds.
Reviewer-identified: human-guided evolution supplies strong changing semantic objectives and favors symmetry, compressibility, and recognizable parts, so Picbreeder is not an unsupervised reference.

Reviewer-identified: NEAT changes topology and nonlinearities while the comparator optimizes weights in a fixed dense final architecture, confounding search objective, curriculum, architecture, sparsity, and optimizer.
Reviewer-identified: the 256-by-256 full grid is a finite sample, not literally every point in the continuous input space, and no held-out coordinates or higher-resolution evaluation are reported.
Reviewer-identified: calling the procedure stochastic gradient descent is imprecise because every iteration uses the full set of pixels; minibatch noise is absent.

Reviewer-identified: no matched L1, weight-decay, group-sparsity, pruning, equivariance, augmentation, curriculum, modular, architecture-search, or alternative-optimizer baseline tests easy mitigations.

Reviewer-identified: evolved networks are effectively sparse and use only a small subset of layerized capacity, while replicas are unconstrained dense solutions; representation density is not controlled.
Reviewer-identified: weight sweeps are manually selected and visually judged; all-sweep data are external, with no aggregate semantic independence, symmetry, smoothness, or output-validity statistic.
Reviewer-identified: local editability in weight space is not a measure of learnability under the training optimizer and may reflect parameter scale or saturation rather than conceptual modularity.
Reviewer-identified: PCA and four random directions do not resolve function-preserving reparameterization ambiguity or demonstrate that no linear or nonlinear basis reveals reusable concepts.
Reviewer-identified: arbitrary rotations are not generally valid between elementwise nonlinear layers; a legitimate hidden-unit basis change requires coordinated transformations of adjacent weights.
Reviewer-identified: the ReLU experiment lacks a functionally matched evolved ReLU UFR, sweep metrics, seed intervals, and comparable sparse or symmetry-aware solutions.
Reviewer-identified: no experiment measures held-out generalization, compositional generation, adaptation speed, continual learning, interference, creativity, robustness, or scaling.
Reviewer-identified: the CPPN-to-LLM analogy maps a low-dimensional deterministic coordinate function to a stochastic high-dimensional sequence model without validating which properties transfer.
Reviewer-identified: the LLM examples use tiny prompt samples and closed versioned products, with no decoding controls, model internals, replication across families, uncertainty, or preregistration.

Reviewer-identified: output inconsistency alone cannot distinguish FER from data imbalance, tokenization, routing, sampling, instruction interpretation, safety layers, or ordinary generalization error.

Reviewer-identified: cited Othello and arithmetic heuristic studies concern particular trained models and do not establish that the same concepts are redundantly implemented across contexts in general.

Reviewer-identified: the paper does not engage deeply with disentanglement identifiability results, standardized factorization metrics, modular-network theory, or causal representation learning that already formalize parts of UFR.
Reviewer-identified: Figure 25 is captioned as butterfly networks although the rendered sweeps depict skulls, a minor but concrete presentation inconsistency.
failure_modes: A human observer prefers sparse symmetric maps and labels them UFR even when another basis or factorization is equally reusable.
A dense solution is classified as fractured because it distributes a feature, although distributed coding improves robustness or capacity through superposition.
A single evolved weight looks semantic only because its scale, downstream saturation, or activation function creates a smooth low-rank perturbation.
Human selection directly rewards symmetry and modular edits, then the resulting inductive bias is misattributed to open-endedness itself.
The evolving architecture has sparse gates and privileged sinusoidal or Gaussian features that the fixed dense optimizer cannot rediscover from random weights.
A trained network contains a unified concept in a rotated or overcomplete subspace but per-neuron images make it look entangled.
A representation is functionally reparameterized by neuron permutation, scaling, duplication, or splitting and receives a different FER judgment despite unchanged adaptability.
Selected sweep examples exaggerate separation while the full distribution of evolved weights contains many destructive directions too.
A local parameter direction is visually editable but gradients for a later task do not find or preserve that direction.
A symmetry-aware or sparsity-regularized gradient baseline reaches a similarly modular solution, invalidating broad claims about conventional objectives.
More training data improves observed behavior while either unifying circuits or merely covering fractures, and the proposed diagnostics cannot distinguish the two.
A prompt contrast fails because one context is rare in training or decoding is stochastic, but the behavior is interpreted as evidence of two internal algorithms.
A mixture-of-experts model isolates tasks while duplicating shared primitives across experts, improving one UFR dimension and worsening another.
Aggressive unification merges mechanisms that should remain context-sensitive, causing negative transfer or erasing legitimate exceptions.
An open-ended training process optimizes novelty without retaining competence, safety, reproducibility, or scalable resource efficiency.
open_questions: Can FER and UFR be defined as basis- and reparameterization-aware properties of functions, circuits, interventions, or task families rather than activation aesthetics?
Which quantitative decomposition separately measures redundancy, context-specific fracture, causal entanglement, modularity, and semantic completeness?
Do FER metrics predict compositional OOD generalization, edit locality, sample efficiency, continual-learning interference, or creative search after controlling for loss and capacity?
How prevalent are UFR-like solutions across the full Picbreeder archive, users, phylogenies, targets, and random or objective-driven evolutionary controls?
Which causal factor matters most: human selection, changing objectives, novelty, topology growth, activation evolution, sparse connectivity, curriculum, or indirect encoding?
Can dense and sparse networks be compared at matched active parameter count, path norm, function complexity, output error, and nonlinear basis?
Do weight decay, pruning, symmetry-equivariant layers, low-rank constraints, modular regularizers, or staged curricula let gradient training recover the known evolved solution?
Can a function-preserving alignment method determine whether two networks encode the same reusable factors under different superposition arrangements?
Can intervention-based tests identify whether one causal mechanism is reused across contexts without requiring a neuron to be monosemantic?
When is redundancy harmful fracture versus useful error correction, ensembling, biological degeneracy, or distributed robustness?
Does adding diverse target instances cause gradual unification, sudden grokking, or increasingly accurate FER, and how does this scale with data and width?
Can curricula be learned from gradient conflict, readiness, causal prerequisites, or minimum-description-length improvement rather than manually ordered?
Can models intentionally consolidate duplicate circuits during training while retaining exceptions, uncertainty, and performance?
How do transformers, attention, residual streams, sparse MoE routing, retrieval, recurrence, and external memory change fracture and entanglement?
Can open-ended problem generation be combined with SGD at foundation-model scale with measurable representational benefits and bounded cost or risk?
What preregistered behavioral and causal benchmark would distinguish FER from tokenization, data frequency, sampling, and generic OOD failure in LLMs?
reusable_insights: Equal benchmark loss does not imply equal editability or future learning; compare functionally matched solutions under downstream interventions.
Keep redundancy and entanglement separate: one asks whether a mechanism is duplicated across contexts, the other whether changing one factor causally changes another.
Representation claims should be invariant to neuron permutation and scaling and explicit about the larger class of allowed basis or circuit transformations.
Use causal activation or weight interventions plus downstream task outcomes, not activation visualization alone, to assign semantic responsibility.
Report the full distribution of intervention effects across parameters, seeds, and targets with blinded semantic ratings or automatic ground-truth factor metrics.
Factorial experiments must separate optimizer, objective, curriculum, topology, activation functions, sparsity, human supervision, and data coverage.
A toy domain is most useful when it includes held-out combinations and future tasks, so representation quality can be tested rather than inferred from appearance.
Include simple symmetry-aware, sparse, modular, pruning, and curriculum baselines before concluding that an optimization paradigm intrinsically prefers fractured solutions.
Treat superposition and distributed representation as possible efficient codes, not pathology by default; harmful fracture requires a demonstrated failure under reuse or intervention.
Use matched function error, active capacity, path norm, and parameter scale when comparing local edit directions across networks.
Behavioral prompt contrasts can generate hypotheses, but internal fracture requires mechanistic tracing and replication under controlled decoding and data-frequency conditions.
Open-ended search is a promising source of curricula and diverse stepping stones, but its representational contribution must be disentangled from human taste and architecture evolution.
Representation consolidation should be evaluated for negative transfer: unifying superficially similar mechanisms can erase contextually valid exceptions.
Measure whether representation metrics predict actual optimization trajectories on later tasks; local semantic smoothness alone is insufficient.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization via Forced Rendering of Disentangled Latents
competitive_landscape.relationship: strongest direct concurrent formalization and empirical extension
competitive_landscape.difference: Liang et al. study an equally visual two-dimensional generator but define factorization in intermediate activations, diagnose layer-by-layer re-entanglement with learned kernels and a Jacobian metric tensor, evaluate genuinely held-out coordinate combinations, and causally improve OOD composition through architecture, regularization, or curated stripe data. This operationalizes the core FER intuition far more directly. The FER paper contributes the open-ended-evolution contrast and a broader conceptual vocabulary, but does not measure compositional generalization or isolate a remedy.

competitive_landscape.title: Breaking Neural Network Scaling Laws with Modularity
competitive_landscape.difference: Boopathy et al. formalize modular task structure, prove a dimension-independent sample-complexity advantage over monolithic kernels under their assumptions, learn module projections, and evaluate in-distribution and compositional OOD generalization including Compositional CIFAR-10. It directly tests the claimed link from factorization to generalization and offers a gradient-based learning rule, narrowing the novelty of UFR's motivation. FER remains broader about redundancy, open-ended curricula, creativity, and continual learning.

competitive_landscape.title: How Diffusion Models Learn to Factorize and Compose
competitive_landscape.difference: Liang et al. use controlled two-dimensional Gaussian generators to show that conventionally trained diffusion models can form factorized semi-continuous manifolds, connect their sudden emergence to percolation, and relate factorization to compositional generation. This challenges any broad inference that gradient training normally yields only FER and supplies quantitative training-stage evidence. It also finds limitations in interpolation, so it supports the narrower concern that apparently compositional models can retain representational gaps.

competitive_landscape.title: Wasserstein Distances, Neuronal Entanglement, and Sparsity
competitive_landscape.difference: Sawmya et al. propose a numerical neuronal-entanglement indicator, identify highly non-Gaussian influential neurons in actual LLM layers, and split their input-output relation into sparse experts to preserve accuracy under pruning. The measure captures only one aspect of FER and is neuron-distribution based, but it is scalable, causal enough to connect to accuracy, and evaluated on modern language models rather than inferred from prompts.

competitive_landscape.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.difference: Chanin et al. identify feature splitting and feature absorption, where a general feature fails to activate in specific contexts and more specific latents absorb its direction. They provide toy proofs, sparse-probe F1 jumps, absorption rates, and causal ablations across Gemma, Llama, and Qwen SAEs. This closely matches fractured context-specific redundancy and offers the measurable phenomenon FER lacks, although it diagnoses SAE decompositions rather than proving that the base model itself uses harmful duplicate mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Superposition disentanglement of neural representations reveals hidden alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: Longon et al. develop theory showing that different superposition arrangements can make functionally related representations appear misaligned, then use sparse autoencoders to reveal stronger DNN-to-DNN and DNN-to-brain alignment. This directly sharpens the paper's unresolved basis objection: apparently disorganized neurons can encode aligned features in different mixtures. FER's weight-sweep evidence concerns parameter editability rather than cross-model alignment, so both diagnostics should be combined.

competitive_landscape.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: Huh et al. survey and measure increasing alignment across architectures and modalities as models scale, proposing convergence toward a shared statistical model of reality. The FER paper directly challenges the inference that such performance and alignment mean internally reusable mechanisms. Platonic alignment metrics can themselves be scale-confounded and need not imply causal circuit unity, but FER supplies no large-scale metric that overturns the convergence evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Locatello et al. prove that unsupervised disentanglement is impossible without model and data inductive biases, train more than 12,000 models across six methods and seven datasets, and find that disentanglement scores do not reliably select models or reduce downstream sample complexity. This directly cautions that UFR needs an explicit semantic inductive bias and demonstrated benefit, not visual naturalness. Picbreeder provides such human bias implicitly but does not quantify or generalize it.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a novel holistic hypothesis: conventional fixed-objective deep learning tends to split reusable concepts into redundant context-specific fragments and entangle independent capabilities, while open-ended search can approach a unified factored representation whose organization supports generalization, creativity, and continual learning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The side-by-side CPPN atlas is unusually vivid. Because every sampled input and every hidden unit is rendered, it communicates a real and often neglected fact: two low-loss parameterizations can have sharply different local edit geometry and apparent modularity. Layerization provides a known good solution inside the comparator's broad architecture, three images reproduce the visual pattern, ReLU replicas weaken one activation-function objection, and the authors are admirably explicit that the work is a hypothesis-generating position paper. Yet nearly every stronger conclusion remains untested. FER and UFR are not operationalized; selection, architecture, sparsity, curriculum, and optimizer are confounded; examples and sweeps are qualitative; basis ambiguity remains; no downstream adaptation is measured; and prompt anecdotes cannot identify circuits. Existing disentanglement, modularity, superposition, sparse-autoencoder, and compositional-generalization work already supplies metrics, theory, and interventions for major parts of the idea.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The durable novelty is the memorable synthesis and the function-matched open-ended-evolution visual counterexample, not a demonstrated law of SGD or foundation models. The research program becomes strong if FER is decomposed into measurable causal reuse, redundancy, and interference; evaluated under reparameterization-aware alignment; and shown to predict held-out composition and future optimization at matched capacity. A decisive experiment would factorially vary objective openness, human selection, curriculum, topology growth, activation family, sparsity, and optimizer on many procedural targets with known factors, then test new compositions and continual tasks. At LLM scale, feature-splitting and absorption metrics, causal circuit tracing, and context-transfer interventions are more credible than isolated prompt failures.
